notes: Concept met: a generic gray humanoid robot seen from directly behind in a pitch-black navy studio. One thin straight blue-white line of light comes down from the top edge, along the back of the skull, and ends in a glowing port at the base of the skull (the nape). Matches the IMG-8 spec and the variant prompt.

Portrait 941x1672 = 0.5628, which is 9:16 (0.5625) to within a rounding error. This is ChatGPT's native 9:16 output size: the other short variants (AI vs ML IMG-1/IMG-4) are the same size, and the longform's own stills are 1672x941. Remotion scales it up about 1.15x to 1080x1920, which is normal for this pipeline and not a defect.
No text, words, logos or watermark. I zoomed the nape and skull and brightened all four corners 4x: nothing. The small raised bracket above the port is a molded latch, not a glyph.

Nothing important is clipped. The head and port are fully in frame with about 400 px of headroom. The beam leaving the top edge is intended (it comes from above). The shoulders and upper arms running off the left and right edges are normal chest-up framing, not a cut-off.

Not blank: mean luminance is 22/255 (a dark look on purpose) and the beam is the one bright accent (1.2% of pixels above 200). The palette matches the longform and vertical IMG-8 (navy-black with a cool blue glow), so it fits next to the F5 face and the C25 receipt.

Variety rule met: this is a clearly NEW composition (centered rear view, straight vertical beam into the nape) compared with the vertical's IMG-8 (three-quarter rear view, curved stream into a side-of-head port). It is not a near-duplicate.

Caption and UI safe: the focal port sits at about 49% height, centered. The short's added captions (bottom-center) land on the mid-dark back panels, where white text with a black stroke will read cleanly. Nothing important sits on the right-hand platform UI rail.
No AI anatomy artifacts: the neck cables and vertebra segments are symmetric and continuous, the two ear discs match, and the panel seams are coherent.
Minor, not a fail: the beam runs ON TOP of the skull surface (nothing hides it) before it meets the port. Over a 2.4 s push-in it reads as light feeding into the head.
